key_insight: Lifting improves mid-circuit measurement reliability by combining repetition-encoded readout signals with neural decoding and in situ calibration to better discriminate quantum states under hardware noise.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical readout stack for superconducting quantum processors, helping make error correction and outcome-dependent control more robust during long-running circuits.
method: Encode target and auxiliary qubit I-Q signals into a joint measurement representation
Train a neural decoder on context-matched, in situ calibration data
Use theoretical analysis to bound risk and support overlap reduction under richer signal channels
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated experimentally across three IBM processors on repeated stabilizer measurement, parity-check, and teleportation workloads.
watch_item: The approach depends on additional readout channels and context-specific calibration, which may increase hardware overhead and require retraining as execution conditions drift.
paper_title: Lifting: Quantum State Discrimination Framework for Mid-Circuit Measurements
